newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 2.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Department of Health says over 300 persons were injured by firecrackers and six killed by stray bullets at the peak of the New Year celebration on December 31 based on reports from 28 hospitals. Newspapers quoted Health Minister Carmencita Reodica noting a dramatic decline in the number of those killed or hurt compared to previous years. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- President Fidel Ramos intends to make 1997 an "exciting workaholic" year" despite his doctors' advice to slow down, as he is eager to conquer "challenges" to his administration's success. (MANILA TIMES)
- More than 26 million workers in the private sector and 1.4 million in government service return to work today after a long New Year's holiday that stretched to a total of five days. (BULLETIN)

- Police agents conduct round-the-clock stakeout operations against Congressman Romeo Jalosjos, charged with the statutory rape of an 11-year old girl, who is believed holed up in a condominium in Pasig City, east of the capital. (MALAYA/STANDARD/INQUIRER)

- The Bankers Association of the Philippines proposes changes in the country's foreign exchange regulations which include an increase in the amount of foreign currency a bank can sell to "walk-in" clients from $25,000 to $1 million. (PHILIPPINE STAR)

- The Department of Finance says the government expects to raise 470 billion pesos in total revenues from various tax and non-tax measures this year, 21 percent higher than the 389.5 billion pesos raised in 1996. (CHRONICLE/TIMES JOURNAL)
- The Board of Investment says government has scaled down its 1997 investment target from 550 billion pesos to 475 billion pesos but did not explain why. (MANILA TIMES)
- Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson says the central bank is set to propose changes in the 47-year old General Banking Act that disallows banks from providing loan guarantees. (INQUIRER)

- Food and beverage conglomerate RFM Corp ventures into economic zone development through its subsidiary RFM Properties and Holdings Inc which will develop a 133-hectare area in Santo Tomas Batangas, south of Manila. (BUSINESSWORLD)

- Oil refiner Petron Corp and First Philippine Holdings Corp are set to conduct a feasibility study on the viability of putting up an oil and gas pipeline and a depot in Bulacan, north of the capital. (BUSINESSWORLD).

- The Central Bank has rejected a proposal from the World Bank to impose a reserve requirement on foreign currency deposit units (FCDUs), fearing that such a measure would trigger widescale withdrawals from these dollar accounts. (BUSINESS DAILY)

- Senate president Ernesto Maceda said the Senate is inclined to support moves to drop controversial issues in the proposed Comprehensive Tax Reform Package and concentrate on individual income tax reforms and improvement of tax administration. (BUSINESSWORLD)
